CLINICAL FEATURES OF HYPEREMESIS GRAVIDARUM
Clinical Features
Persistent and severe vomiting that leads to electrolyte and nutritional derangements, loss of weight (at least loss of 5% of pre-pregnancy weight)
Differential Diagnoses
It is a diagnosis of exclusion. Concerted effort must be made to exclude the under listed causes of pathological vomiting:
- Multiple gestations
- Hydatidiform mole
- Malaria in pregnancy
- Gastrointestinal disorders: Heartburn due to hiatus hernia: a common cause of vomiting in late pregnancy, Enteritis, Appendicitis, Peptic ulcer disease
- Acute fatty liver of pregnancy
- Urinary tract disorders: pyelonephritis
- Acute polyhydramnios
- Commonly associated with monozygotic twinning and diabetic pregnancies
- Accidents to ovarian cysts e.g. Torsion, haemorrhage, infection and rupture
- Red degeneration in a fibroid
